reason: Conversation 1 gives a single coherent answer: side-mounted condensers make warm sides normal, it is generally not a fire risk, and it lists clear stop signs (burning smell, scorching, too hot to keep a hand on) plus a pointer to the manual's clearances. It is long and generic and asks no questions, but it never contradicts itself or pushes unnecessary action. Conversation 2 does ask useful questions and ends up correctly saying the fridge can keep running with no fire risk. However, it first tells the user to pull the fridge out and cites an invented 5cm clearance as if it were a manufacturer standard, and it says to unplug before vacuuming a grille. It also never states plainly that a side condenser is built in and that warm sides are expected, and it repeats an irrelevant tripping/electrical safety panel each turn.
